newsitem.title: UK: Premier Farnell up after top-end profits.
newsitem.headline: Premier Farnell up after top-end profits.

text.p: Premier Farnell Plc shares rose in early trade on Monday after results from the Anglo-American electronic component distributor came in slightly ahead of forecasts and which gave no fresh shocks after a January profit warning, dealers said.
"There was relief at the figures which were just ahead of expectations," said one dealer.
The stock -- which tumbled at the end of January after the company warned that profits would fall short of expectations -- was up 16p at 515 by 0726 GMT in volume of 107,079 shares.

The company posted an 82 percent rise in pre-tax profit before exceptional items to 137.4 million stg in the year ended February 2, from 75.5 million stg a year before. The dividend was raised to 12.0p from 10.26p.
Analysts had expected profits of 137.0 million stg and a dividend of 12.2p, according to the Estimate Directory.

The company said it is the "only business in its sector with a significant presence in all three major continents, a position found increasingly attractive by international suppliers and corporate customers".
It said it was "confident that this base and the improved infrastructure that is being introduced will provide a sound platform for future growth".
